diagnostic_evidence.quote: The trial  functions $\{ \phi_{i,j} (x,y) :=\phi _i(x)\phi^j(y) \} _{i,j=1}^{N-1,M-1} \in S^N,$ are simply a tensor product of  one dimensional hat functions.

Motivated by (\cite{arXiv}), the test functions  $\{ \psi_{i,j} (x,y) :=\psi _i(x)\psi^j(y) \} _{i,j=1}^{N-1,M-1}\in T^N$ are a tensor product of exponential basis functions in the horizontal and hat functions in the vertical direction.

issues.failure_explanation: A second-order ODE has two undetermined constants, but the displayed condition only prescribes one value and also mixes the indices through $\psi_i(x_j)=\delta_{i,j}$. A single global exponential cannot satisfy the required nodal basis conditions either; the intended piecewise local boundary conditions are missing. Thus the test space $T^N$, and hence the finite-element solution $U$ in the discrete weak form, is not well-defined as written.

failure_location.quote: the basis functions $\psi _i(x)$ are the solutions of \begin{eqnarray*} \ve \frac{\partial ^2 \psi _i}{\partial x^2}  + \bar a_i (y_j) \frac{\partial  \psi _i}{\partial x} =0, \quad \psi _i(x_j) = \delta _{i,j}. \end{eqnarray*}

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define each horizontal test function piecewise on the two elements adjacent to its node as a solution of the displayed ODE with two local nodal conditions, and correct the interpolation condition to $\psi_i(x_l)=\delta_{i,l}$; this recovers the intended exponential-spline finite-difference scheme.
issues.overall_effect: The finite-element formulation underlying the main theorem is ill-posed as stated. The associated finite-difference scheme is separately defined and is the object actually used in the subsequent analysis.
issues.title: Horizontal exponential test functions are not uniquely defined
issues.why_classification: The repair is a standard local definition of the intended exponential splines and does not alter the analyzed scheme, rates, or scope.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: the vertical mesh distributes  $M$ mesh points in the ratio $1:2:1$ across the three subintervals $[0,\tau _y]$, $[\tau _y,1-\tau _y]$ and $[1-\tau _y,1]$.

issues.failure_explanation: The last branch of $B_2$ is inconsistent with the value $1$ at $y_j=1-\tau_y$; the natural correction is division by $\tau_y$, not $1-\tau_y$. Even after that correction, the fine transition step is $k_fine=4\tau_y/M$, so $-\varepsilon\delta_y^2B_2=\varepsilon/(\tau_y k_fine)=M/(16\varepsilon(\ln M)^2)$ at the transitions, not $\sqrt{\varepsilon}M/(8\ln M)$.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the last branch by $(1-y_j)/\tau_y$, replace the asserted action by $\varepsilon/(\tau_y k_fine)$, and recalibrate the $B_2$ coefficients locally; the same component bounds can then be recovered.
issues.overall_effect: The barrier constants calculated from the asserted action of $B_2$ are wrong in the proofs of Lemmas lem:added-3 and lem:added-4, and consequently the barrier argument behind the main global bound is not justified as written.
issues.title: Vertical barrier B2 is misdefined and its asserted discrete action is false
issues.why_classification: This is a local barrier recalculation and coefficient adjustment; it requires no new construction and preserves the stated bounds.

issues.failure_explanation: Direct substitution of $Z_i=e^{2x_i/\alpha}$ into Corollary Cor1 gives a positive term of the form $\sigma(2h_i/\alpha)e^{2h_i/\alpha}$, up to the positive factor $(1-e^{-\bar\rho_{i+1}})^{-1}$, not $\sigma(2h_i/\alpha)^{-1}$. The exponential factor in the negative term is also different from the one displayed. Thus the written estimate is not a valid consequence of Cor1.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the displayed consequence of Cor1 by the direct substitution, or by a standard direct Taylor/fitted-operator estimate for $e^{2x_i/\alpha}$; this is a contained correction and preserves the intended barrier.
